semantics.binding: Yumu binding resolution uses event.sender.contactID (sender.user_id) via BindDao.getBindFromQQOrNull / UserIDUtil; top-level event.user_id is NOT used for group-message binding. Changing sender.user_id would break binding.
semantics.permission: PermissionImplement.isBlock and CheckAspect use event.sender.contactID + event.group.contactID (group_id). Sender identity mutation would break permission/admin checks.
semantics.pendingPromptWaiter: AsyncMessageUtil keys are group:<group.contactID>:<sender.contactID> and are notified by AsyncMessageUtil.put(event) which runs inside PermissionImplement.onMessage — i.e. only after the Shiro dedup filter passes. A dropped event can never notify a waiter.

semantics.commandHistory: QQMessageCacheProvider keys are (message_id, group_id, sender.user_id) with 2-minute/24-hour TTLs; sender identity mutation would corrupt history attribution
semantics.userState: GroupDao mode/state uses group_id; per-user state (bindings, permissions) uses sender.user_id
semantics.replyRouting: group replies route via Group(bot, group_id).sendMessage over the same WS session; top-level event.user_id is not used as a reply target for group messages
semantics.eventTimeConsumers: exactly two consumers of event.time in the Yumu app: (1) Shiro 2.5.3 dedup key, (2) OneBotListener.kt stale gate (time<1e10 branch; drop when now-time>30). The Yumu event wrapper API (qq/event/Event.kt, qq/event/MessageEvent.kt) does not expose time, so application services cannot read it.
semantics.verdictOnSenderMutation: REJECTED: any design that changes sender.user_id breaks binding, permissions, waiters, history and user state.
semantics.verdictOnTimeMutation: ALLOWED with constraints: synthetic event time is consumed only by the stale gate and the dedup key; the fix must stay inside the stale gate tolerance for the yumu target.

structuralClassification.method: for a synthetic key S, every real triple that can equal S has T_r = first 10 chars of S (10-digit epoch seconds), then G_r = S[10..10+gl) and U_r = S[10+gl..) for some gl in 1..10; a split is valid only when neither G_r nor U_r starts with '0' and U_r has <=10 digits
quickRouterPath_Gs_770099: same-user class: T_r = T_s div 1000, G_r = dec(X)+'770099' (9 digits, X = T_s mod 1000, X in 100..999 -> groups 100770099..999770099), U_r = U_s
different-user class: T_r = T_s div 1000, G_r = dec(X)+'77009' (8 digits), U_r = '9'+dec(U_s) (10 digits) when |U_s|<=9
executorSameGroupPath: same-user: impossible for any user length (13-digit T_s vs 10-digit T_r with identical G suffix)
different-user: possible only when G_r is 3-periodic and starts with X (e.g. 123123 or 123123123 with X=123) AND |U_s|<=7, so U_r = dec(X)+dec(U_s) fits 10 digits

leadingZeroLemma.statement: if X = T_s mod 1000 < 100, the first digit of any forced real-group split is '0'; for a real group message group_id > 0 and group/user ids use canonical decimal representations without leading zeros, so no valid real triple can equal the synthetic key for any group/user digit length
leadingZeroLemma.proof: key equality forces T_r = first10(S) (real epoch seconds are exactly 10 digits); G_r starts at char 11, which is the first char of X; a positive canonical decimal group_id string starts with 1..9
leadingZeroLemma.verifiedExhaustively: all X in 0..99 over user lengths 6..12: zero valid splits
leadingZeroLemma.costIfEnforced: only 100 unique synthetic times per aligned second -> would require per-second queueing/fallback under >100 bridge calls/sec; NOT selected

practicalRiskAssessment.quickRouterVirtualGroupPath: collision requires a real event from the same user, in one of 900 nine-digit groups ending 770099 whose 3-digit prefix equals the call's millisecond residue, at wall second T_s div 1000 (two seconds after the call second with margin 2000), within the 5s cache window; conditional probability <=1/1000 per same-second coincident real event; expected incidence negligible at this deployment's volume
practicalRiskAssessment.executorSameGroupPath: same-user collision impossible; different-user collision requires a 3-periodic real group id AND a <=7-digit sender id (QQ ids are normally 9-10 digits)
practicalRiskAssessment.conclusion: candidate A remains safe with the corrected wording and these explicit bounds; it eliminates the live-confirmed Wuxin-Wuxin failure and reduces Wuxin-vs-real risk by >=1000x versus baseline seconds

allocatorStress.gate: Yumu OneBotListener ms branch: drop iff receiveNow - eventTime > 30; there is NO future bound
allocatorStress.sameMsBurst5000: monotonic, never past, all pass gate at +10ms receive delay; future drift = margin + N - 1 = 6999ms; drift decays 1ms per wall-ms
allocatorStress.wallRollback5000: next time stays strictly increasing; drift 7001ms; gate passes (diff negative); drift fully decays after ~5002 wall-ms
allocatorStress.wallForwardJump: only gate failure mode: in-flight forward jump F drops the first call of a burst iff F > 2030ms (F=2030 passes, F=2031 drops)
allocatorStress.burstBudget: call i in a same-ms burst has budget 2030+i ms (first call 2030ms; 6th call 2035ms)
allocatorStress.naiveAllocatorVsCap: naive allocator CAN exceed any fixed semantic future cap (40k same-ms burst -> drift 41999ms > 30000ms; large rollback likewise)
allocatorStress.revisedAllocator: adds a hard 30000ms future-drift guard; in the current control flow rollback fail-fast is actually enforced by the safe-pool boundary (poolLast check fires before the drift check), and the 30s guard is effectively unreachable because safe-slot values are only 2000..3098ms ahead. It is kept as a defensive/future-proof guard, not as the current rollback mechanism.
allocatorStress.maximumSafeDrift: gate-derived bound: past drift <=30ms at Yumu receipt, and allocator past drift <=0 at allocation (never trips); future drift is gate-unbounded but the safe-pool window bounds normal drift to <=3098ms. The 30000ms check is defensive/future-proof and dominated by the pool boundary check in current control flow.
allocatorStress.allocatorExceedsBound: naive: yes (unbounded burst/rollback); revised: no, it rejects instead
